evidence.claim: Putin signed a law extending uniform remote electronic voting rules across elections and referendums and shifting practical regulation to election authorities.
evidence.title: Putin signs law, spreading electronic voting to all elections
evidence.excerpt: Putin signed a law extending uniform remote electronic voting rules across elections and referendums and shifting practical regulation to election authorities.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Contemporaneous wire report on a signed federal law with direct political effects.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Directly attributable to Putin because he signed the law
contrary_evidence: Officials framed the law as modernization and convenience.
The practical effect was to expand a voting channel critics said was easier to manipulate.

evidence.claim: The chair of the CEC said no international observers would be invited for the regional elections because the legislation did not envisage them, and EPDE described a rigid legal interpretation that blocked observation.
evidence.title: No international politically-biased observers identified during the 2022 Russian regional elections
evidence.excerpt: The chair of the CEC said no international observers would be invited for the regional elections because the legislation did not envisage them, and EPDE described a rigid legal interpretation that blocked observation.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Specialized election-monitoring analysis with direct institutional description.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Attributable to the Russian electoral system under Putin's control
contrary_evidence: The CEC presented the rule as a legal constraint, not a political choice.
The effect still reduced transparency and outside scrutiny.

evidence.claim: Golos said the 2022 elections could not be recognized as truly free because of unequal campaigns and restrictions on the right to stand for office and on basic political rights and freedoms.
evidence.title: Statement on election observation on the Single Voting Day September 11, 2022
evidence.excerpt: Golos said the 2022 elections could not be recognized as truly free because of unequal campaigns and restrictions on the right to stand for office and on basic political rights and freedoms.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Primary election-monitoring statement from Russia's best-known domestic observation movement.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Attributable to the regime under Putin through the electoral framework and enforcement environment
contrary_evidence: The state still held formal elections.
Golos's conclusion is that formal voting existed without real contestability.

evidence.claim: A new law that entered into force on December 1 dramatically expanded the foreign-agent regime, making it easier to designate critics and excluding them from key civic and political activities.
evidence.title: Russia: New Restrictions for 'Foreign Agents'
evidence.excerpt: A new law that entered into force on December 1 dramatically expanded the foreign-agent regime, making it easier to designate critics and excluding them from key civic and political activities.
evidence.source_locator: opening paragraphs and explanation of the law's effects
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Detailed legal analysis by a major human-rights organization on a specific 2022 statute.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Attributable to Putin's government and legislative majority
contrary_evidence: Officials said the law protected sovereignty and security.
The practical effect was to widen exclusion and chill opposition activity.

evidence.claim: A Russian court banned Facebook and Instagram after finding Meta 'extremist', deepening the blockade on major independent information channels.
evidence.title: Russian court bans Facebook and Instagram after Meta found 'extremist'
evidence.excerpt: A Russian court banned Facebook and Instagram after finding Meta 'extremist', deepening the blockade on major independent information channels.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Reuters report of a formal court ban and extremist designation.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Attributable to the Russian state under Putin
contrary_evidence: Meta had changed its policies in response to the invasion.
The Russian ban was still a broad political-information restriction.

evidence.claim: CPJ reported that Russian authorities revoked Novaya Gazeta's online license only days after the paper's print license was stripped, removing nearly all remaining space for the outlet to operate in Russia.
evidence.title: Russian authorities revoke Novaya Gazeta's online media license
evidence.excerpt: CPJ reported that Russian authorities revoked Novaya Gazeta's online license only days after the paper's print license was stripped, removing nearly all remaining space for the outlet to operate in Russia.
evidence.source_locator: opening paragraphs and quoted CPJ statement
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Direct press-freedom monitoring report with explicit description of the state action and its impact.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Attributable to the Putin-controlled regulatory and judicial system
contrary_evidence: The timing and scope strongly suggest political suppression.

evidence.claim: Putin signed the federal law on monitoring persons under foreign influence, consolidating foreign-agent provisions and defining the designation broadly enough to cover people receiving foreign support and engaging in political or information activity.
evidence.title: Law on monitoring activities of persons under foreign influence
evidence.excerpt: Putin signed the federal law on monitoring persons under foreign influence, consolidating foreign-agent provisions and defining the designation broadly enough to cover people receiving foreign support and engaging in political or information activity.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Official Kremlin publication summarizing the signed law and its operative scope.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Direct personal attribution to Putin as the signing authority
contrary_evidence: The Kremlin said the law improved legal regulation and transparency.
The law still materially widened tools for political exclusion and censorship.

evidence.claim: The Council of Europe said Russia ceased to be a party to the European Convention on Human Rights on 16 September 2022, ending a major external legal avenue for complaints and judgments.
evidence.title: Russia ceases to be party to the European Convention on Human Rights
evidence.excerpt: The Council of Europe said Russia ceased to be a party to the European Convention on Human Rights on 16 September 2022, ending a major external legal avenue for complaints and judgments.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Official Council of Europe notice on the legal cutoff date and its consequences.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Attributable to the Russian state under Putin, though caused by Russia's expulsion and withdrawal process
contrary_evidence: The Court retained residual jurisdiction for earlier acts.
That residual jurisdiction did not restore the lost domestic remedy path.

evidence.claim: Putin backed constitutional changes that reset his term count and allowed him to remain eligible to rule until 2036.
evidence.title: Putin approves changes allowing him to stay in power until 2036
evidence.excerpt: Putin backed constitutional changes that reset his term count and allowed him to remain eligible to rule until 2036.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Contemporaneous Reuters report on the constitutional reset and its effect on term limits.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Directly attributable to Putin's constitutional redesign
contrary_evidence: Putin publicly said he favored term limits in a politically mature system.
The practical effect was still to remove normal succession pressure.

unresolved_gaps: Direct evidence on command-and-control discipline, custody, accident-prevention, and other nuclear safety procedures in 2022 is thin.
Direct evidence on expert governance and risk institutions is weak relative to the rhetoric and escalation evidence.
The package needs better household and distribution evidence, not just macro stabilization and state-budget outcomes.
Direct evidence that appointments and institutions translated into durable productivity investment is still thin.
Direct 2022 delivery evidence for health, education, housing, and food security inside Russia remains thin.
Implementation and take-up by region and group are not well documented.
Direct documentary proof of Putin's personal beneficial ownership, asset control, or hidden conflicts remains limited.
The appointment and accountability map is still too thin for a fully rounded honesty judgment.
Direct 2022 implementation metrics for procurement, output, and battlefield effectiveness remain thin.
The package still needs a cleaner separation between frantic adaptation, temporary stabilization, and genuinely effective goal advancement.
